status_summary: On 2025-09-19 DOL launched Project Firewall, an H-1B enforcement initiative under which the Secretary of Labor personally certifies the start of investigations where there is reasonable cause to suspect noncompliance, led by the Office of Immigration Policy, ETA and the Wage and Hour Division; violations can lead to back wages, civil penalties or debarment from the H-1B program. On 2026-07-08 the DOL Office of Inspector General announced a major investigation into fraud and human trafficking in the H-1B and PERM programs with federal law enforcement partners. DOL debarment lists show H-1B debarments with periods beginning from 2025-05-12 to 2026-09-24 and dozens of H-2A, H-2B and permanent certification debarments beginning in 2025 and 2026. Neither release mentions faster debarment or exclusion from federal contracts, and action on the 2020 Inspector General recommendations was not found.

timeline.event: DOL announces Project Firewall: H-1B enforcement initiative with Secretary-certified investigations and possible debarment (Release No. 25-1476-NAT).

The DOL Office of Inspector General announces a major investigation and stepped-up enforcement against fraud and human trafficking in the H-1B and PERM programs, working with federal law enforcement partners and the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud; the release does not mention debarment.
H-1B debarment period begins for the latest of six entries on the Wage and Hour Division list (earliest start 2025-05-12); the page was last updated 2026-09-30.

title: Step up visa fraud investigations and debarments of abusive foreign labor employers
uncertainties: The Project Firewall release and the Inspector General press release of 2026-07-08 were read in full on dol.gov and oig.dol.gov on 2026-10-18; the H-1B debarment list was read by the researcher this run and in an earlier review. The OFLC debarment list (54 entries) was read in an earlier review; its start dates are not necessarily final-order dates, and the lists show only current debarments, so speed cannot be judged. A DOL accomplishments page reportedly cites nearly 200 Project Firewall investigations with no stated date; it was not opened in review and is not cited. September 2026 PERM suspensions were seen only in a law-firm report that links a social media post; no primary release was opened, so no event was added. The Inspector General's 2020 report and any DOL response were not located. Project Firewall targets H-1B compliance generally, which overlaps with but is not the same as visa fraud.
